# PERITONITIS ASSOCIATED WITH PERITONEAL DIALYSIS

Peritonitis associated with peritoneal dialysis usually presents with abdominal pain, fever, nausea or vomiting, and cloudy effluent. The leukocyte concentration is greater than 100 cells/microliter of dialysate, with more than 50% neutrophils.

Obtain Gram stain, culture, and cell count with differential of dialysate before antimicrobials are given. Nephrology consultation is essential. If cultures show Gram-negative or mixed bacterial infection, a gastrointestinal tract infectious source is more likely. Gram-positive organisms like staphylococci usually result from external contamination. Fungal peritonitis is rare and requires immediate catheter removal.

\*\*Antimicrobial recommendations are for empirical therapy only. Regimens should be tailored according to patient response and microbiology results in consultation with Nephrology and/or Infectious Diseases for more information.

To prevent catheter occlusion by turbid dialysate, add 1,000 units of heparin per dialysis bag each day until one day after the dialysate is clear. If vancomycin is used, trough serum concentrations should be kept above 15 mcg/ml to ensure adequate intraperitoneal levels. Usually vancomycin must be given every 3 to 7 days. Contact Nephrology and/or Pharmacy for more information.

## Consult Nephrology in all cases.

## Antimicrobial therapy

## Duration

Duration of therapy depends on the pathogen identified. Treat staphylococcal and streptococcal infections for 2 weeks and all other gram-positive infections for 3 weeks. In patients who have Staphylococcus isolated and had a previous staphylococcal infection, treat for 3 weeks.

Therapy:
## All antimicrobials below are administered via peritoneal dialysate bag over 6 hours with the option to include heparin 1000 units.

## Empirical treatment while waiting for results of gram stain

[Cefepime 1 gm PD q24h ($$) [R]](pd-cefepime-1gm-q24h)
<OR>
[Cefazolin 15 mg/kg ($) [R] <AND> gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg ($) [R,O] PD q24h](pd-cefazolin-15mg-kg-gentamicin-06mg-kg-q24h)
MRSA risk factors
Vancomycin 30 mg/kg PD LD then 15 mg/kg PD every 3 to 7 days ($) [R] <AND> cefepime 1 gm PD q24h ($) [R]
Alternative for severe penicillin or cephalosporin allergy [Vancomycin 30 mg/kg PD LD then 15 mg/kg PD every 3 to 7 days ($) [R]](pd-vancomycin-15-30mg-kg-q5-7d) <AND> gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg PD q24h ($) [R,O]

## Gram positive organism

[Cefazolin 15 mg/kg PD q24h ($) [R]](pd-cefazolin-15mg-kg-q24h)
< OR >
Vancomycin 30 mg/kg PD LD then 15 mg/kg PD every 3 to 7 days ($) [R]

## Gram negative organism

Cefepime 1 gm PD q24h ($$) [R]
Alternative for severe penicillin allergy
Gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg PD q24h ($) [R,O]

## Alternative treatments for narrowing coverage based on isolate susceptibilities

Cefazolin 15 mg/kg PD q24h ($) [R]
< OR >
[Ceftazidime 1 gm PD q24h ($) [R]](pd-ceftazidime-1gm-q24h)
< OR >
[Ceftriaxone 1 gm PD q24h ($) [M]](pd-ceftriaxone-1gm-q24h)
< OR >
Gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg PD q24h ($) [R,O]
< OR >
Vancomycin 30 mg/kg PD LD then 15 mg/kg PD every 3 to 7 days ($) [R]

## Antifungal prophylaxis:

Antifungal prophylaxis may be used for the duration of antimicrobial therapy to possibly reduce the risk of fungal peritonitis.
Fluconazole 200 mg PO every other day ($) [R,DI]
<OR>
Fluconazole 100 mg PO q24h ($) [R,DI]
